transcript:
This message comes from Odoo, the all-in-one business management software platform.
Whether you're a small or large business, Odoo gives you one flexible platform built to grow with you.
Try today for free at odoo.com/nprpodcasts.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
President Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections today from Florida, not Washington, D.C.
When asked if he voted the party line, the president said, "Very much so."
He's now in Georgia, speaking on behalf of GOP candidates in that state.
Former President Obama headlined a rally in Cleveland today to boost the Democratic candidates for governor and U.S. Senate.
IDEA streams Conor Morris reports.
So I'm asking you, are you fired up? Are you ready to go?
Obama took aim at Trump and Republican allies U.S. Senator John Husted and Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy.
He said change starts in Ohio with Democrat Sherrod Brown trying to win back a Senate seat and Ohio Democrat gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton.
This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration.
Obama laid blame at the president's feet for rising costs.
The former president made the stop ahead of another rally for Democratic candidates in Michigan.
For NPR News, I'm Conor Morris in Cleveland.
In some states, today was the last chance to register to vote for the midterm elections.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has a list of the upcoming deadlines.
The window is closing today for eligible voters in Massachusetts and New York to register or update their registration.
And we are now one week away from Halloween on October 31st,
which is also the last day in North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's early voting sites.
The only state where voter registration is not required is North Dakota,
and many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on November 3rd's election day.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election website
to confirm your status and contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
An $800 million agreement has been reached with the Archdiocese of New York involving child sex abuse and Pierre Chantaliz Duster.
The Archdiocese of New York says it has agreed to settle sexual abuse claims brought against the church.
Archbishop Ronald Hicks said in an email to Archdiocese pre-Saturday afternoon that they are on the verge of being able to
"bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim survivors."
Jeff Anderson, an attorney for some of the plaintiffs, told NPR 1300 people accepted the $800 million agreement.
It really is a testament to the courage and the persistence of the survivors who stood up, who spoke up, and who caused the Archdiocese of New York
to finally reckon to each of them, which is long past due.
Anderson also says survivors feel relief about the settlement and sorrow about the abuse they faced.
Chantaliz Duster, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
New data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention find birth rates in the U.S. fell to their lowest level ever recorded last year.
The CDC also found a big shift toward older women choosing to have children.
NPR's Brian Mann reports.
Final CDC data shows a 1 percent drop in U.S. birth rates, continuing a decline that began 20 years ago.
Researcher Brady Hamilton says the eye-catching drop in 2025 came among younger women in their late teens and 20s.
A 6 percent decline in the birth rate for women 20 to 24 is noteworthy.
Experts say career and financial pressures are causing many women to have fewer children later in life.
Dr. Denise Branch in OB-GYN at Temple Health in Philadelphia says older maternity can be good for women and babies if they have medical support.
I see the net positive as being the fact that we have a choice.
Falling birth rates mean fewer children in the U.S. According to the U.S. Census, the population under age 18 has dropped steadily for more than a decade.
Brian Mann, NPR News.
Quest Diagnostics reports it learned of a cyber breach of one of its systems this week, which the medical laboratory operator says has likely compromised some patient records.
The unauthorized access affected Quest's Quantum Lab Services Manager. The full extent of the breach is still under investigation.
Quest confirmed this breach is unrelated to recent code vulnerabilities.
Cyberattacks are increasing among many industries, prompting global efforts to enhance online security.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, Washington.
This giving season, your support brings health and hope to families worldwide.
Learn more or donate today at internationalmedicalcorps.org/npr.

topics.text: Trump votes in Florida midterms and says he voted the party line
Obama rallies in Cleveland for Democratic Senate and governor candidates Brown and Acton
States report upcoming voter registration deadlines, with North Dakota requiring no registration
Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement of child sex abuse claims
CDC data shows U.S. birth rates fell to record low in 2025, mostly among younger women
Quest Diagnostics reports cyber breach of a system likely exposing some patient records
